component.name: SoundText
component.summary: Write music as text, then hear, arrange and mix it
Scrivi la musica come testo, poi ascoltala, arrangiala e mixala
Écrire la musique en texte, puis l'écouter, l'arranger et la mixer
Escribir música como texto, y luego escucharla, arreglarla y mezclarla

description.p: SoundText is a music editor where music is written as plain text: notes, chords, dynamics and form in a small notation language. The note being played lights up in the text, and the same song can be seen as a score.

ul.li: A notation checked bar by bar while you type, with patterns and transformations
An arranger that writes drums, bass and comping from a chord track
A structure view where each section of the song is a box of text
SoundFont and SFZ instruments, LV2, VST3 and CLAP plugins, NAM amplifier profiles
Audio tracks, and converting a recording into notation
Export to WAV, MIDI, MusicXML and PDF

description.p: Songs are plain text files in the open ST-language format, which also has a standalone Python library and command-line tools.

screenshot.caption: A song in the structure view, with the mixer

description.p: Songs in 60 seconds sound more coherent, with an automatic harmony check and a phone app with instrument packs.

ul.li: Song in 60 seconds: melody and coloured chords agree, fills and crashes at section changes, a second voice over the chords, and a lineup checked genre by genre
New harmony check (python -m core.harmony_check song.st) that finds melody notes clashing with bass and accompaniment
More genres and moods, swing, borrowed chords and chord symbols in the Generate windows
SoundText Mobile: instrument packs in SF3 and a reduced General MIDI sound base

description.p: A whole song in 60 seconds, a more readable generated text, richer generators and screen reader support.

ul.li: New song in 60 seconds: 25 genres, each with its own instruments, scales, accompaniment styles and starting effects
Generated text written in bars with patterns for repeated bars, and a Human control for each style's micro-timing

Generators: borrowed chords and other cadences, inversions with the bass following them, a pedal bass in the bridge, a theme taken up an octave in the last chorus with a second voice in thirds, pickup notes, string layers and an energy curve
Screen reader: every control has a name, Where am I?, next and previous error, and listening to the note or the bar under the cursor
Downloads of third-party plugins are checked against fixed versions and SHA-256 hashes

description.p: CLAP plugins get their own window and saved state, and the Flatpak installs instruments properly.

ul.li: CLAP plugins open their own graphical interface and keep their internal state in the song
Download and install: guitars, amplifier models and CLAP plugins, with 7z archives supported
Flatpak: downloaded instruments are kept after closing the program
The option to hide CLAP plugins that also exist as VST3 is always visible and remembered
Score view button next to Structure and Text; the toolbar rearranges on narrow windows

description.p: Audio output through JACK, CLAP plugins, and packages for Arch Linux and Flatpak.

ul.li: Sounds → Audio output → JACK: SoundText becomes a JACK client with its own ports
CLAP effects and instruments, next to LV2, VST3 and Audio Unit
The same song now renders to the same audio with FluidSynth 2.4 and later
MusicXML files with unusual time signatures (3/3, 4/6) can be imported

description.p: Audio Unit plugins and a ready-made app for macOS.
